profile.ledger: One body came to me, in a coat too large for it, with two men's names attached. I am still not certain which of them I collected.
profile.ledger_beaten: He apologised to everyone at the table, and asked me not to mention it to his friends. I have not. Some of them are already with me.
history: Henry Jekyll, M.D., D.C.L., LL.D., F.R.S., of Robert Louis Stevenson's Strange Case of Dr Jekyll and Mr Hyde (1886): a large, well-made, smooth-faced man of fifty, with every mark of capacity and kindness, who gives good dinners in a handsome old house in a square. Behind it stands the dissecting theatre he bought from a celebrated surgeon's heirs, and its blistered door opens on a by-street. Convinced that man is not truly one, but truly two, he mixed a draught that set his lesser half loose in a body of its own, and called him Edward Hyde. He took rooms for him in Soho, told his servants to obey him as they would their master, and made a will leaving him everything.

His friends are few and loyal: Utterson the lawyer, who would not stop asking; Lanyon, who saw the change with his own eyes and did not survive the shock; Poole, the butler, who heard the wrong voice behind the cabinet door. The salt that fixed the draught ran out, and the new supply would not serve; the first had been impure. He wrote his full statement under the last of the old powders, locked in his cabinet, and was never seen again. He accepted this invitation on condition that he would come as himself. Nobody can promise him that any more, the dealer included.
profile.at_the_table: Tight and patient. He comes into few pots, folds to a big raise without a real hand, and is plainly sorry to be playing at all; he seldom bluffs and bets small when he bets. But once he has put a share of his stack in, he will not be bet out of the pot: he sees things through, which has always been his difficulty. Losses get under his skin faster than his manners suggest, and when he tilts he plays like a looser, rougher man.
profile.look: Silhouette: large and well made, upright, broad-shouldered, a little heavy at fifty. Smooth-faced and clean-shaven, a fine forehead, dark hair greying and neatly brushed, the face of a respectable physician with something tired at the eyes. A dark frock coat, a grey waistcoat with a watch chain across it, a black cravat, a white handkerchief. Hands large, firm, white and comely. Prop: a small glass phial of blood-red draught standing on the felt by his hand; picking it up is the tell surface.
profile.public_domain: Stevenson's novella (1886) is public domain. Build him from the text only: a large, smooth-faced, kindly gentleman of fifty. No likeness of any actor who has played him (Barrymore 1920, March 1931, Tracy 1941 or later), no top hat and opera cape from the stage versions, no bubbling laboratory of coloured flasks, no green potion, and nothing from The League of Extraordinary Gentlemen. One phial, blood-red, as Lanyon found it.

fold: I shall stand aside. Forgive me.
Fold. Discretion is the better part of medicine.
I withdraw. It is a habit I am trying to keep.
check: Check. I am in no hurry.
call: Call. A respectable man pays what he owes.
I will see it. I have come too far to turn back.
Call. I have signed for worse.
Call. Once I begin a thing, I see it through. That is my difficulty.
bet: Bet. In moderation, as in all things.
I shall venture a little. Forgive the liberty.
raise: I raise. I hope I give no offence.
Raise. Pray do not think it unlike me.
Raise. Even a careful man must sometimes be bold.
all_in: All of it. God forgive me.
Everything. I have nothing more to keep back.
The whole of it. I had meant to keep a little back. I always do.
